newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello wants more labour reform - report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello wants more labour reform - report.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello has warned there will not be a significant fall in unemployment without further deregulation of the labour market, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Friday.

The newspaper said Costello had made it clear during an interview that he believed the industrial relations reforms, which started to take effect earlier this month, would not substantially reduce unemployment, currently at 8.6 percent.
"He suggested that this will happen only if there is enough flexibility for wages to go lower as well as higher," the newspaper said.
"His comments on industrial relations reform are the strongest indication from anyone in the government that another wave of labour market changes will be necessary."
The newspaper said Costello had cited the United States, New Zealand and Britain as reaping the benefits of greater labour market flexibility.
"We are not as flexible as them and that's one of the reasons why we have a higher unemployment rate," he was quoted as saying.
The Australian parliament last year passed the conservative government's workplace reforms, which aim to deregulate the labour market and give unions a less significant role in wage negotiations.
However, Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Thursday there were no plans to introduce further reforms as the government was concentrating on implementing the legislation.
